title: The Forms of Shiva and Vishnu
translation: With the noose, goad, snake, ḍamaru drum, skull-cup, trident, skull-staff, spear, arrow and bow, ten objects held in his hands and exchanged from hand to hand, how many different forms of Shambhu (Shiva) are there? And likewise of Hari (Vishnu), with the four: mace, discus, lotus and conch?
translation_hi: पाश, अंकुश, सर्प, डमरू, कपाल, त्रिशूल, खट्वांग, शक्ति, बाण और धनुष, इन दस वस्तुओं को अलग अलग हाथों में बदल बदल कर रखने से शंभु (शिव) के कितने रूप बनते हैं? और इसी प्रकार गदा, चक्र, कमल और शंख से हरि (विष्णु) के कितने रूप बनते हैं?

words.note: Same word as in the peacock verse.
The instrumental plural ending -aiḥ covers the whole compound list.
Also 'power'. In Hindi physics, शक्ति = power.
Also 'arc' in geometry: चाप = arc of a circle.
From √yu (to join). Compare yutiḥ in the peacock verse.
Present tense plural of √bhū (to be, become).
anyonya (mutual) + hasta (hand) + kalita (held): swapped hand to hand.
mūrti (image, form) + bheda (difference). Hindi मूर्ति, भेद.
Literally 'enemy'; a name for the cakra, the enemy of demons.
Instrumental plural, closing the second list.

grammar: One ending for a long list: पाशाङ्कुशाहिडमरूककपालशूलैः is one dvandva compound. Only the last word takes the case ending (-ऐः); all the others share it.
Visarga to r: शम्भोः + हरेः + इव → शम्भोर्हरेरिव. After a vowel other than अ/आ, visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound.
Upapada compound: सरोज = सरस् + ज, 'lake-born'. Same pattern: जलज, पङ्कज (lotus), द्विज (twice-born).
Genitive: शम्भोः, हरेः 'of Shambhu, of Hari'. The forms belong to the god, so the god takes the 'of' case.
question: How many different forms of Vishnu are there?
solution:
The first hand can hold any of the 4 objects, the second any of the 3 left, then 2, then 1:

4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 4! = 24 forms of Vishnu

For Shiva's ten objects: 10! = 10 × 9 × … × 1 = 3,628,800 forms

Science link: this is the factorial, n!, the number of ways to arrange n things. In the Lilavati it comes from the अङ्कपाश (aṅkapāśa) chapter on permutations. In your puja: the 24 names recited during ācamana and sandhyā (केशव, नारायण, माधव, गोविन्द…) are traditionally the 24 forms of Vishnu, each told apart by the order of śaṅkha, cakra, gadā and padma in his four hands. Exactly 4! = 24.
